title: WHOIS and RDAP Expose Different Views of Registration Data

cover.h1: WHOIS and RDAP Expose Different Views
cover.subtitle: Protocol access does not make every identity public.
cover.visual: Two lookup views share one registration card while personal fields remain hidden.

sections.name: 01-protocol
sections.heading: RDAP changes the access method without promising a public identity directory
sections.scene: Three layers show protocol, authoritative source, and client presentation. Personal contact card remains visibly restricted.
sections.alt: Protocol, source, and presentation form separate parts of a lookup.

sections.name: 02-fields
sections.heading: Public fields support registration checks rather than complete ownership conclusions
sections.scene: A public result card connects registrar and event fields to supported questions, with identity question kept separate.
sections.alt: Public registration fields support limited conclusions.

sections.name: 03-redaction
sections.heading: Redaction notices explain an information limit rather than an empty registration
sections.scene: A complete registration file has a public view with clearly marked hidden personal fields, without displaying personal values.
sections.alt: A redacted public view differs from an absent registration.

sections.name: 04-request
sections.heading: Contact and disclosure requests need a separate purpose and process
sections.scene: Four labeled routes separate purchase inquiry, abuse report, account recovery, and nonpublic-data request.
sections.alt: Different registration questions follow different contact routes.

purpose: Initial illustration plan. The final image review manifest records actual asset hashes and visual revisions.
